🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Wednesday, 25 November 2026

1. ⚡ Energy bills are to rise by 26% from January
A household using a typical amount of energy would see its annual bill rise from £1,723 to £2,166 if this level was sustained for a year.

2. 💷 Government-commissioned disability benefit review calls for closer link with costs
A government-commissioned report calls for a "rebalancing" of the amount paid to different disability benefit claimants, linking it more closely to their costs.

3. 🔪 Government to take forward plans for knife seller licensing scheme
The planned scheme would cover businesses and private sellers of knives, with the aim of keeping dangerous weapons off the streets.

4. 📊 Study finds widespread misperceptions on immigration among the public
A new study found a widespread lack of knowledge of the actual level, scale and nature of immigration to the UK.

5. 🏛️ Burnham confirms independent panel on health legacy of Cold War nuclear tests
The prime minister says a Hillsborough-style independent panel will examine the health legacy of Britain's Cold War-era atomic programme. He says nuclear test veterans will get the full truth.

6. 🌡️ Record 5,200 heat-linked deaths are estimated in England this year
The UK Health Security Agency says this year's number of deaths is twice that of the previous record year.

7. 🚔 Report finds racism, misogyny and homophobia remain in the Met
A new report has found institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia still exist in the Metropolitan Police, three years after a damning review.

8. 💰 Millions of people will receive a £100 energy payment from January
An explainer sets out whether people will get the £100 energy payment and when it will arrive. Millions are due to receive it from January.

Sources: BBC, GOV.UK Home Office, Sky News. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Prime Minister's Office / OGL 3, Wikimedia Commons.
